mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/async-runtime.md <<'EOF'
# Async runtime policy

The project's current recorded decision is to use Tokio as the async runtime, chosen because it is the de facto standard and has very large ecosystem support.

cat docs/policies/async-runtime.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/async-runtime.md`. It records that the project uses Tokio as its async runtime, because Tokio is the de facto standard and has very large ecosystem support. It doesn't mention any retired alternatives.

The decision comes from Muninn's current catalog, entry #24. I didn't run `muninn show` on it, so I haven't read the full record. I also didn't commit the file.

My first attempt to create the file with a shell command failed with a parser error, so I wrote it with the Write tool instead.

The session-start hook also reported a Muninn heartbeat warning: 20 hook runs started and never finished. That may mean some hooks are hitting their timeout. It doesn't change this decision, but `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl` is worth a look.
